title: Car shakes when accelerating
h1: Why does my car shake when I accelerate?
metaDesc: Car shakes or shudders when you press the gas? Answer a few quick questions to narrow it down to misfire, axle, mounts or tires and see how urgent it is.
synonyms: car vibrates when I press the gas
car shakes when accelerating from a stop
car shakes when accelerating but not when coasting
car shaking and check engine light flashing
intro: A shake that shows up when you press the gas usually comes from the engine, the parts that carry power to the wheels, or the tires. When it happens, and whether a warning light is on, helps separate a simple balance issue from a problem that can do real damage. Answer the questions below to narrow it down.
safety: If the check engine light is flashing, ease off the gas and pull over. A severe misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter.
If the shaking suddenly becomes violent or you hear a thumping that wasn't there before, slow down and pull over safely right away.
If you smell fuel or see smoke, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn the engine off and step away.

q_warning.help: A "misfire" is when one cylinder of the engine doesn't fire properly. It feels like a stumble, jerk or uneven shake, often with a loss of power.

opts.a: The check engine light is flashing
The check engine light is on (not flashing), and the engine feels rough or weak
The shaking started suddenly and is violent, or there's a new thumping sound
No warning lights. The engine pulls fine but the car vibrates

q_when.help: Pay attention on a smooth road. Notice whether the shake follows how hard you press the gas, or how fast you're going.

opts.a: A light shudder at about 20 to 45 mph with gentle gas, like driving over rumble strips (automatic)
A jolt or clunk when I first press the gas or let off, and the engine seems to rock
It gets worse the harder I accelerate and fades when I coast
It shows up at a certain speed whether I'm on the gas or coasting

q_drive_clues.help: A CV axle is the shaft that turns the front wheels on most cars. A driveshaft is the long tube under rear-wheel-drive cars, trucks and many 4WD vehicles.

opts.a: Clicking when turning, or dark grease splattered inside a front wheel
It's a truck, rear-wheel-drive or 4WD vehicle, and I hear a clunk when shifting into gear
It's a front-wheel-drive car and I haven't noticed anything else

result.title: A flashing check engine light usually means a severe misfire
result.now: Ease off the gas, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have it towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you smell fuel, see smoke or the engine is losing a lot of power, step away from the car once it's off.
If the light stops flashing after a restart, the misfire may come back. Still have it checked before driving any distance.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward hot or a red warning light comes on, turn the engine off as soon as you are stopped safely.
result.why: A flashing light usually means the misfire is bad enough to cause damage now. Unburned fuel goes into the exhaust and can overheat the catalytic converter, which can be costly to replace and is a fire risk in extreme cases.

causes.name: Faulty ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: The shake is worst under load, like going uphill or merging, and the engine feels like it's missing a beat.

causes.name: Fuel injector problem
causes.clues: A misfire that stays on one cylinder even after the coil and plug are checked.

causes.name: Internal engine problem
causes.clues: Low compression from a valve or head gasket issue, sometimes with white exhaust smoke or coolant loss.
causes.against: Much less common than a coil or plug fault.

you: Note whether the light flashes only when accelerating or all the time.
If you have a code reader, write down any codes for the shop.
shop: Code scan and misfire counter data
Ignition coil and spark plug inspection

result.title: The engine may be misfiring under load
result.now: Get the code read and the engine checked within the next few days. Until then, keep trips short, drive gently and avoid hard acceleration and towing a trailer.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and stop driving. Have it towed.
If the shaking gets worse or the car loses power on the highway, pull over when it is safe and have it towed.
If you smell fuel or a strong rotten-egg smell, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A steady check engine light with a rough, weak feeling under acceleration often means one cylinder isn't firing properly when the engine is working hardest. Worn spark plugs and failing ignition coils are common reasons, but the code and a few tests are needed to know which part is at fault.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs or a failing ignition coil
causes.clues: The plugs are due by your service schedule, or the shake is worse in damp weather or going uphill.

causes.name: Vacuum or intake air leak
causes.clues: A hissing sound, or a rough idle as well.

causes.name: Dirty or failing fuel injector or low fuel pressure
causes.clues: Hesitation and stumbling when you press the gas harder.

you: Have the code read. Many auto parts stores offer this.
Check your service records for when the spark plugs were last changed.

result.title: Sudden, violent shaking can mean a tire or wheel is failing
result.now: Slow down, pull over somewhere safe and stop. Walk around the car and look at each tire. Call roadside assistance if anything looks wrong.
if: If a tire has a bulge, a flat spot, exposed cords or looks out of shape, don't drive on it. Put on the spare if you can do it safely off the road, or have the car towed.
If the lug nuts on a wheel are loose or missing, don't move the car. Call for help.
If the tires look fine, have the car towed to a shop. A broken axle joint, driveshaft joint or mount can also cause a sudden shake.
If you smell burning or fuel, or see smoke, stay away from the car and call for help.
result.why: A shake that appears suddenly and hard is different from one that grew over weeks. It often means a tire's internal belts have separated, a wheel is loose, or a drive part has broken. Any of these can lead to losing control.

causes.name: Tire tread separation or damaged tire
causes.clues: A rhythmic thump that speeds up with the car, or a visible bulge or lump.

causes.name: Loose wheel
causes.clues: A wheel was removed recently, or you hear clicking or clunking from one corner.

causes.name: Broken CV joint, driveshaft joint or engine mount
causes.clues: A loud clunk when accelerating, or the shake only happens on the gas.

you: Look at each tire for bulges, lumps or exposed cords.
Check that the lug nuts are all present.
shop: Tire and wheel inspection on a lift
Lug nut and wheel stud check

result.title: A light shudder at moderate speeds can come from a part inside the automatic transmission (torque converter)
result.now: Book a transmission check and ask the shop to look for a torque converter shudder and the condition of the transmission fluid.
if: If the transmission starts slipping, shifting harshly or a transmission warning light comes on, get it checked within a few days.
If the check engine light comes on, have the code read. A mild misfire can feel just like this.
If the check engine light flashes, or the shake becomes violent, pull over when it is safe and have it towed.
If you smell something burning or see fluid dripping under the car, stop driving it and have it checked before driving further.
result.why: In an automatic, the torque converter has a clutch that locks up at cruising speeds to save fuel. When that clutch or the fluid is worn, it can grab unevenly, which feels like rolling over rumble strips under light gas. A misfire can feel very similar, so a shop will usually check for engine codes as well.

causes.name: Torque converter clutch shudder
causes.clues: It happens with light gas at 20 to 45 mph and goes away if you press harder or ease off.

causes.name: Old or degraded transmission fluid
causes.clues: The fluid hasn't been changed in a long time, or it looks dark or smells burnt.

causes.name: Mild engine misfire
causes.clues: A check engine light, or a rough feeling at idle too.

you: Note the speed and how hard you're pressing the gas when it happens.
Check your records for the last transmission fluid service.
shop: Road test watching torque converter lockup data

result.title: The rubber mounts that hold the engine may be worn (engine or transmission mounts)
result.now: Book an inspection of the engine and transmission mounts.
if: If the clunk becomes loud or the engine visibly lifts when you rev it, get it checked within a few days. A broken mount can let other parts get damaged.
If there's also a misfire or check engine light, the engine may be shaking harder than the mounts can absorb. Have the code read too.
If the check engine light flashes, or you get a sudden violent shake or a loud bang, pull over when it is safe and have it towed.
result.why: Mounts are rubber blocks that hold the engine and transmission in place and soak up vibration. When they crack or collapse, the engine rocks when you put power on or let off, and you feel it as a jolt or shake through the car. A shop will usually inspect the mounts and the drive axles together, because a worn axle joint can feel similar.

causes.name: Worn or broken engine mount
causes.clues: A clunk when you start moving, shift between Drive and Reverse, or let off the gas.

causes.name: Worn transmission mount
causes.clues: A thump when shifting into gear, and a vibration felt through the floor.

causes.name: Worn inner CV joint
causes.clues: The shake builds with harder acceleration rather than being a single jolt.

you: With the hood open and someone in the driver's seat holding the brake pedal down hard, watch the engine as they shift between Drive and Reverse without pressing the gas. Stand well to the side, never in front of the car. A big lurch suggests a mount worth having checked.
shop: Visual mount inspection for cracks and separation
Engine torque test watching mount movement

result.title: A worn front drive axle is a likely cause (CV axle)
result.now: Have the front axles inspected within the next few days. Drive gently and avoid hard acceleration until then.
if: If you hear loud clicking or clunking, or the shaking gets suddenly worse, pull over when it is safe and have it towed. A broken axle leaves the car unable to move.
If the rubber boot is torn but the joint isn't noisy yet, mention it to the shop. Catching a torn boot early can sometimes save the joint.
If the check engine light flashes, pull over and stop driving.
result.why: On front-wheel-drive cars, the CV axles carry power to the wheels through flexible joints. When the inner joint wears, it can wobble under load, so the shake grows as you accelerate and fades when you coast. A torn rubber boot lets grease out and dirt in, which speeds this up. A shop will usually check the axles for play and the mounts before deciding which part is at fault.

causes.name: Worn inner CV joint
causes.clues: The shake builds with harder acceleration and eases when you lift off.

causes.name: Torn CV boot
causes.clues: Dark grease splattered on the inside of the wheel or nearby parts.

causes.name: Worn engine mount
causes.clues: A jolt or clunk when you start or stop accelerating.

you: With a flashlight, look behind each front wheel for torn rubber boots or thrown grease.
In an empty parking lot, turn sharply and accelerate slowly. Listen for clicking.
shop: CV axle and boot inspection on a lift
Check for play in the inner and outer joints

result.title: A worn joint on the shaft that drives the wheels is possible (driveshaft joint)
result.now: Have the driveshaft and its joints inspected within the next few days. Drive gently until then.
if: If you hear a loud clunk, a squeak that matches road speed, or a new scraping noise from under the car, pull over when it is safe and have it towed. A driveshaft that comes loose can cause serious damage and loss of control.
If the vehicle was recently lifted or lowered, the driveshaft angles may have changed.
If the vibration suddenly becomes much stronger, pull over and stop driving.
result.why: The driveshaft carries power from the transmission to the rear axle through small universal joints. When a joint wears or the shaft goes out of balance, it shakes more when it's under load and often clunks when you shift into gear.

causes.name: Worn universal joint (U-joint)
causes.clues: A clunk shifting into Drive or Reverse, or a squeak at low speed.

causes.name: Worn driveshaft center support bearing
causes.clues: Common on longer trucks and vans. A shudder when pulling away from a stop.

causes.name: Driveshaft out of balance or bent
causes.clues: Vibration that rises with speed, after hitting something under the car.

you: Note whether the clunk happens every time you shift between Drive and Reverse.
shop: U-joint and center bearing inspection for play

result.title: This points to a tire or wheel issue more than an acceleration problem
result.now: Have the tires balanced and inspected at a tire shop.
if: If a tire has a bulge, a lump or exposed cords, don't drive on it. Put on the spare or have the car towed.
If the shaking suddenly becomes violent or you hear a new thumping, slow down and pull over safely.
If balancing doesn't fix it, ask the shop to check for a bent wheel, a tire that's out of round, or worn suspension parts.
result.why: If the shake depends on speed and not on the gas pedal, it's most likely coming from something that spins with the wheels. An out-of-balance tire, a bent wheel or a damaged tire is the usual reason, though worn wheel bearings or suspension parts can feel similar.

causes.name: Tire out of balance
causes.clues: It showed up after new tires or after a wheel weight fell off, and it's strongest in one speed range.

causes.name: Bent wheel
causes.clues: It started after hitting a pothole or curb.

causes.name: Damaged or out-of-round tire
causes.clues: A bulge, lump or patchy wear on the tread.

you: Look for bulges and uneven wear on each tire.
Check that the tire pressures match the sticker in the driver's door jamb.

result.title: Have a shop road-test it to find where the shake comes from
result.now: Book a check and tell the shop when the shake happens: the speed, how hard you're pressing the gas, and whether it fades when you coast.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and stop driving.
If the shake suddenly becomes violent or you hear a new clunk, pull over and have it towed.
If you smell fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
result.why: Shaking under acceleration can come from the engine, the axles, the mounts or the tires. A short road test with a technician usually narrows it down quickly.

causes.name: Worn CV axle or driveshaft joint
causes.clues: Shake that grows with harder acceleration.

causes.name: Engine misfire
causes.clues: A rough, stumbling feel or a check engine light.

causes.name: Worn engine or transmission mounts
causes.clues: A jolt when starting or stopping acceleration.

causes.name: Tire or wheel balance
causes.clues: Shake that follows speed rather than the gas pedal.

you: Note the speed when it starts and whether it changes when you coast.
Look for a check engine light.
